newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends down on hog data, fund sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends down on hog data, fund sales.

text.p: Most corn contracts made fresh contract lows Monday and all ended lower on bearishly interpreted hog population data and commodity fund selling, traders said.
"The market was weak to begin with, and the hogs and pigs report just pushed us lower," said one floor trader.
Corn settled down 2 to 6-1/4 cent per bushel, with March down 6-1/4 cent at $2.58-1/4.

On Friday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture reported that the U.S. hog population was 96 percent of year-ago levels, which stirred concern about diminishing feed demand and pressured futures, traders said.
Commodity funds were said to have sold 22 million bushels of corn, which contributed to the market's weak tone, traders said.

Cargill was estimated to have bought 17 million bushels of March on the day. Traders said that business was linked to Cargill's application with the U.S. Treasuary to barter grain for other natural resources in a deal with North Korea.

Weak weekly export inspection data from USDA also contributed to the soft tone in futures, traders said. The government reported Monday that inspections were 29 million bushels, when trade estimates ranged from 32 to 45 million bushels.

In other trade, Continental Grain, ADM Investor Services and O'Connor Grain each bought two million bushels March. Prudential Securities sold 4.5 million March and Griffin Trading sold three million bushels March.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 42,000 contracts, above the 27,519 traded Friday.
In corn options, Refco bought 1200 March $3.00 calls and Chicago Corp sold 200 March $2.70 puts, trade sources said.
Corn options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 9,000 contracts, above the 4,366 traded Friday.
